reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Enumerated powers, child welfare, custody, and care payments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1) to (19), including (17)(a) and (17)(b)a-c), history note (L. 1945 p. 945 § 33 through A.L. 2014 H.B. 1299 Revision), and the 1998 case annotation (R.J.A. v. G.M.A., 969 S.W.2d 241, stating statute does not authorize division of youth services third-party custody in a dissolution action). Covers legal, contract, property, subpoena, rulemaking, federal-cooperation, advisory-committee, research, child-welfare, juvenile-court cooperation and section 211.031(1)(1)-(2) legal custody evaluation/relief powers, licensed/out-of-state facility care payment limits and 'care' definition, gifts/grants, and cost-of-living guides. Revised during review to specify 'care payments' rather than bare 'payments'.

headings.title: Applying powers and duties to other laws
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history note, and the 1998 case annotation (R.J.A. v. G.M.A.). Extends all children's division powers and duties, so far as applicable, to administering any other law or state law imposing duties on the division acting as a state agency. Revised during review to include both powers and duties and avoid narrowing 'any other law or state law' to state laws alone.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 207.020:10932, all subdivisions (1)-(19) including (17)(a)-(b)a-c, subsection 2, history note (1945 through 2014 H.B. 1299 Revision), and the 1998 R.J.A. v. G.M.A. annotation on third-party custody in dissolution actions; verified all source and body fingerprints. Revised subsection 1 to specify 'care payments' and subsection 2 to cover both powers and duties under any other law or state law.

headings.title: Enumerated division powers and public welfare services
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1) to (15)) and history note (L. 2014 H.B. 1299 Revision). Covers legal, contract, funds/property, subpoena, rulemaking, federal-cooperation, advisory-committee, dependency-prevention, statistics/research, family/needy-person welfare, gift/grant, and cost-of-living budgetary powers; explicitly notes that subdivisions (13) and (15) are verbatim duplicates in the archived source text regarding accepting, selling, and expending gifts and grants.

headings.title: Applying powers and duties to other laws
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2014 H.B. 1299 Revision). Extends all family support division powers and duties, so far as applicable, to administering any other law or state law imposing duties on the division acting as a state agency. Revised during review to include both powers and duties and avoid narrowing 'any other law or state law' to state laws alone.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 207.022:10934, all subdivisions (1)-(15), subsection 2, and 2014 H.B. 1299 Revision history note; verified all fingerprints. Confirmed verbatim source duplication of subdivisions (13) and (15) on gifts and grants is faithfully documented without alteration. Retained subsection 1 title; revised subsection 2 to cover both powers and duties under any other law or state law.

headings.title: Joint county offices and welfare director
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (RSMo 1939 § 9405 through A.L. 2004 H.B. 1453). Covers mandatory joint operation of a county office in every county by the family support and children's division directors, permissive charge by a county welfare director with at least two years' prior Missouri residency, and salary payment from appropriated division funds.

headings.title: Political subdivision agreements, contributions, and deposits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers permissive agreements with political subdivisions to accept moneys, services, or quarters as contributions toward county offices or division duties, with received funds payable to the director of revenue and deposited in a special state treasury account as appropriated division funds. Revised during review so non-monetary contributions (services and quarters) are covered alongside fund deposits.

headings.title: Employment and pay of other county office staff
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers employing additional county office staff with due regard to county population, existing conditions, and purpose, paid like other employees of the family support and children's divisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 207.060:10940, all three subsections, and history note (RSMo 1939 § 9405 through 2004 H.B. 1453); verified all fingerprints. Checked mandatory joint county-office operation versus permissive county welfare director charge and residency/funding rules. Retained subsections 1 and 3; revised subsection 2 to cover non-monetary contributions (services and quarters) alongside fund deposits.

headings.title: Workers' compensation election, self-insurance, and defense
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 353 § 1, A.L. 2014 H.B. 1299 Revision). Covers department of social services authorization to elect chapter 287 coverage under section 287.030 for all department employees, state self-insurer liability without insurance, and attorney general defense of actions against the state as self-insurer.

headings.title: Federal Economic Opportunity Act work-project coverage
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers deeming persons assigned to cooperative state-federal welfare work projects under the Federal Economic Opportunity Act of 1964 (or amendments) to be department employees solely for chapter 287 coverage, provided via insurance or commissioner-of-administration fund deposit using only federal grant funds.

headings.title: Rules classifying eligible employees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers mandatory department of social services rulemaking to classify employees eligible under this section and making that classification decisive as to coverage eligibility.

headings.title: Director authority to carry out section
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Authorizes the director of the department of social services to perform duties necessary to carry out this section effectively.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 207.070:10941, all four subsections, and history note (1965 through 2014 H.B. 1299 Revision); verified all fingerprints. Checked chapter 287 / section 287.030 election, state self-insurance and attorney general defense, Federal Economic Opportunity Act of 1964 work-project coverage funded solely by federal grants, decisive classification rules, and director authority. Retained all four titles as accurate.

headings.title: Dismissal conditions, appeal rights, and contractor definition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history note (L. 2004 H.B. 1453, A.L. 2018 S.B. 1007), and Revisor repeal footnote. Covers dismissal (subject to subsection 2) of child-protective-services employees, supervisors, and private contractors who purposely, knowingly, and willfully violate policy, rule, or directly related state law directly resulting in serious physical injury or death; appeal rights under sections 36.380 and 36.390 for section 36.030(1)(2) positions, if any; and the definition of 'private contractor with the division'.

headings.title: Sections 660.019 to 660.021 and excess-caseload mitigation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history note, and Revisor footnote noting that sections 660.019 to 660.021 were repealed by H.B. 1608, 2012. Preserves the archived cross-reference to sections 660.019 to 660.021 without claiming current enforceability, and covers good-faith efforts as a mitigating factor in dismissal decisions when caseloads exceed Council for Accreditation for Families and Children's Services standards.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 207.085:35407, both subsections, history note (2004 H.B. 1453, 2018 S.B. 1007), and Revisor repeal footnote for sections 660.019 to 660.021 (repealed by H.B. 1608, 2012); verified all fingerprints. Checked qualified dismissal standard, conditional appeal rights under sections 36.030(1)(2), 36.380, and 36.390, private contractor definition, and excess-caseload good-faith mitigation while preserving the repealed cross-reference neutrally. Retained both titles as accurate.
